title: Implement linear aggregate padding on fixed bit tapes
body:
PR2457 explicitly assumes a linear charged scan for aggregate binary padding and restriction. This contribution implements that scan with17fixed bit tapes, one-cell read/write/move primitives, two countdown counters per coordinate, and unchanged canonical descriptors. A written amortized proof gives1024*N+128*sum(L_i)+128 steps per complete scan, including head rewinds and owned-counter cleanup.

The result closes this scan premise only. Fresh owned output/counter intervals and aggregate descriptors are explicit inputs; fast completed exchange, caller parking, descriptor construction, joined physical supplier and stock/kappa admission remain external. The indexed exchange used by tests is a semantic oracle.

Validation: registered optimized CPython3.12 replay;256shapes/49247padded rows;4096Boolean payloads;267counter cases including257-bit carry chains; translated confinement, immutability and cleanup;5semantic controls. Git-free empty-PATH public replay is read-only and rejects actual reset removal, typed receipt corruption and output overwrite. Independent agent machine/proof review found no issue. All9committed files match tested bytes.

Started from current canonical main0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2, priority4; prescribed selected baseline passed. The stock/depth/later-stage candidates were already covered, so TASK explicitly records the changed uniform-transfer scan scope.
